articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially rolled out GPT-5 across ChatGPT and its API, featuring significantly improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a larger effective context window. Benchmarks show substantial gains in graduate-level science, mathematics, and code generation tasks, narrowing the gap with specialized domain models. The model also introduces a new "deep research" agent mode capable of multi-step tool use over extended periods.

articles.title: Google DeepMind Demonstrates Gemini-Powered Robot That Learns Household Tasks from a Single Video
articles.summary: DeepMind published research showing a Gemini 2.5-based vision-language-action model that enables a mobile manipulator robot to learn novel household tasks—such as loading a dishwasher or folding specific garments—from a single human demonstration video. The system generalizes across different kitchen layouts and object configurations with an 87% first-attempt success rate. This represents a major step toward foundation-model-driven generalist robots that require minimal task-specific training.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool-Use Orchestration Framework for Enterprise Agents
articles.summary: Anthropic released a new orchestration layer for Claude that lets enterprises define complex multi-agent workflows with built-in guardrails, audit trails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. The framework supports structured tool calling across databases, APIs, and internal services while enforcing fine-grained permission policies. Early enterprise adopters report 40-60% reductions in back-office process completion times for tasks like procurement and compliance review.

articles.title: Figure and BMW Expand Humanoid Robot Deployment to Third Factory, Citing Productivity Gains
articles.summary: Figure AI announced expansion of its humanoid robot deployment at BMW's manufacturing facilities, with a third plant in South Carolina now integrating Figure 02 units on the assembly line. BMW reports that the robots handle bin-picking, part insertion, and quality inspection tasks with 96% uptime. The expansion makes BMW one of the largest real-world testbeds for general-purpose humanoid robots in industrial manufacturing.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that it has begun risk production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node at its Fab 20 facility in Hsinchu, roughly one quarter ahead of its original roadmap. The node uses gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and backside power delivery, promising 15-20% speed improvement and 25-30% power reduction over the N2 node. Major customers including Apple, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm have taped out test designs, with volume production targeted for mid-2027.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 Behemoth with 2 Trillion Parameters Under Permissive License
articles.summary: Meta released the full Llama 4 Behemoth model—a 2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture—under a permissive open license, making it the largest openly available foundation model to date. The model matches or exceeds several proprietary frontier models on reasoning and multilingual benchmarks. Meta simultaneously released optimized quantized variants and distilled smaller models designed to run on single-node GPU clusters, significantly lowering the barrier for enterprise and research adoption.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Implant
articles.summary: Neuralink announced FDA clearance for its N2 implant, a second-generation brain-computer interface device featuring twice the electrode count of its predecessor and a fully wireless charging system. The expanded clinical trial will enroll up to 50 patients with spinal cord injuries and ALS. Early data from the first-generation trials showed participants achieving cursor control speeds approaching those of able-bodied mouse users, building confidence in the therapeutic pathway.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Electric Demonstrates Autonomous Construction Site Operations
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics showcased its electric Atlas humanoid robot performing autonomous tasks on a mock construction site, including carrying irregular loads across uneven terrain, operating power tools, and coordinating with a Spot quadruped for site surveying. The demonstration used a new planning stack that combines large vision-language models with model-predictive control for whole-body dynamic manipulation. The company announced a pilot program with five major construction firms slated to begin in Q4 2026.
